messages:
alex_sales: Quick question for the thread — customer (POC) asked what our breach notification window is and who gets looped in. They want clear SLAs and handoff steps for their security team. Can we confirm the standard POC workflow?

jamal_se: Short answer: for hosted POCs we follow the standard incident runbook. If customer data is impacted we escalate to security & CS immediately. Tech detail: we keep request/access logs + model inputs for X days (per contract) — I can paste exact retention if needed.

maria_security: Adding specifics from IR: our internal containment window target is <4 hours for confirmed active incidents (high-sev). Investigation and root-cause within 48–72 hours as an initial report. Customer notification: standard advice is to notify affected customers within 72 hours of confirmation that customer-data exfiltration occurred or is very likely.

lena_legal: To clarify: 72 hours is the common regulatory threshold for supervisory authorities under GDPR, but contractual obligations can require faster customer notice. For POCs we usually stick to 72h unless the SOW/contract says otherwise. Sales — check customer contract for any shorter clauses.

alex_sales: Helpful — client is US fintech POC, asking if we’ll do 24-hour notice to their security ops. Can we promise that?

maria_security: We can commit to expedited notification if the contract requires it and we have an agreed escalation channel (dedicated email + phone). Operationally we need: 1) naming of the customer security contact, 2) phone number for urgent calls, 3) whether they want a CSP-style postmortem or a redacted technical annex.

jamal_se: For hosted vs VPC difference: hosted = Redwood operates infra; timeline triggers are internal detection or customer report. VPC/on-prem = customer infra detection is often first signal; notification steps depend on access. In VPC we generally need a legal/ops approval before we push logs out.

alex_sales: So for this customer (hosted POC) they want 24h promise — is that reasonable if we add to SOW?

lena_legal: We can add 24h notification as a contractual SLA for the POC, but we should add carve-outs: must be within our control, and we need permission to share specific log/data elements. Also include an exception for incidents under active law-enforcement gag orders.

maria_security: Also add the practical commitments:
```
- Initial ack to customer security contact: within 1 hour of confirmed incident (low-bandwidth);
- Full initial incident report: within 24 hours (if contract requires), with status and mitigation steps;
- Follow-up technical report / postmortem: within 7–14 days depending on complexity.
- Immediate interim mitigations (if applicable): token/key rotation, model rollback, routing changes.
```

jamal_se: For POC handoff and CS coordination: please always cc: support@redwood.com and cs-<acct>@redwood.com so we can open a ticket and track SLA. Our deploy-bot will create incident ID automatically if you post the severity tag.

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4312 — severity: high — link: https://infra.incidents/redwood/INC-2026-4312 (auto-generated) :robot_face:

alex_sales: Perfect — I'll propose the following to customer: 1) add 24h initial report clause to SOW, 2) provide their security contact + phone, 3) agree to redacted postmortem within 14 days. Anyone object?

lena_legal: Sounds fine. I'll draft a short clause with carve-outs and an approval flow for log disclosure.

maria_security: One more ops note: if the customer wants direct phone alerts to their oncall, we need them to sign an acceptance form for 2FA SMS/call and ensure we have escalation matrix. Otherwise email only.

alex_sales: Got it — I'll collect those details during the next call. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
